summary: Tested Media Store + Percia + Itemizer hookup (backend + frontend). New pytest test_media_percia.py: 14/14 pass. It covers upload with the portal token and with the service key, idempotent re-upload (same media_id, created:false, 1 doc), exact GET fields, a 15-min signed URL (tampered sig 403), time-range overlap filtering, 401 without a key, old /frames 404, Percia 202, idempotent goal_id, exact goal/hit fields, status done, the callback to a local receiver with a valid HMAC and exact envelope, a media url that 404s (403) -> failed/result null, an invalid video -> failed, /percia/frames returns image/jpeg, and a bad-signature callback 401. One E2E run with the real 50 MB HEVC MOV (test_media_percia_e2e.py) passed in about 47 s. The run uploaded 4 MB chunks, then the duration_ms was 43360. vanity_mount resolved to floor (basis seen, conf 0.96). 'Retile under old vanity' was added with basis seen and evidence.frame_url/box, the frame serves as JPEG, all 3 callbacks were delivered (callback_ok true), and chips were filled. Frontend: the portal quote screen shows the camera button seen-frame-btn-it2, the dialog opens with the real frame (768x1366) and an orange box. The dashboard drawer shows drawer-quote with 4 drawer-line rows and the same camera button and dialog. /dev shows 11 dev-video buttons with hidden inputs accept=video/*. Uploading a webm showed 'Uploading 100%', then the toast 'video stored', and the media doc was created. No /frames references remain in the frontend. A live portal call was not tested because VOICE_MODE=vapi needs a real Vapi call; useClipRecorder was code-reviewed only. Regression: test_itemizer.py + test_itemizer_fixes.py gave 36/38. The 2 failures come from this iteration's intended engine/KB changes; the tests were not updated for them.

minor.issue: Fails: Retile item has rule_id 'retile_open_space' instead of 'retile_floating'. Flow: sink gone -> replacing_vanity new -> camera floor. The generalized retile_open_space fires while new_vanity_mount is still unresolved, because the `not` check only excludes an explicit 'floor'. So it wins before new_vanity_mount=floating is answered, and has() blocks retile_floating. The amount/label are the same. The rule also fires early, before the homeowner says whether the new vanity is floor-standing, and gets removed later if they say floor. Decide: update the test to accept either rule_id, or make retile_open_space require new_vanity absent OR new_vanity_mount resolved to floating.

Fails: goal-result returns version None. Cause: new guard in engine.on_goal_result returns early ('already answered by the homeowner') when the fact was resolved with basis said. The earlier test in the same module answered vanity_mount='floor' for the same 'vapi' lead. The behaviour is intended, but the test needs updating (use a fresh lead or a fact not yet said).

Chips get every hit label (up to 2 per met goal), not one per met goal: 3 met goals -> 6 chips, e.g. 'Vanity with sink', 'Clean flooring and cabinetry'. That matches the spec wording 'each met hit's label', but the review request expected one chip per met goal. Pick one.
kw.pop('headers') runs inside the retry loop, so the 2nd attempt (after a 404 re-init) sends the PUT without Content-Type.
The toast always says 'Percia is checking it now' even when no camera goals are open (e.g. all camera facts already resolved), so nothing is sent. Minor UX.

issues: Portrait iPhone frames make the dialog 942px tall in a 1080 viewport. On shorter laptop screens (<=900px) it will overflow without scrolling. Add max-h (e.g. max-h-[70vh] object-contain) on the img. The box overlay must then be positioned against the rendered image box.

'Upload walkthrough video' is offered for every lead, including the real lead Dhivya and deposit_received leads. Consider hiding it for real/past-walkthrough leads to avoid accidental Gemini spend or overwriting a real quote.

Update test_vapi_goal_then_update_scope_same_version for the new 'camera never overrides a said answer' guard.
Decide chips: one per met goal vs every hit label.
Fix storage._call so headers survive the retry.
Optional: cap the SeenFrame image height; hide the /dev video upload for real leads.
critical_code_review_comments: useClipRecorder uses seq = t_start_ms (ms offset), not a counter. That is unique per session but fine only while the clocks agree. t_start is computed from client Date.now() minus the server started_at, so clock skew shifts clip times (Math.max(0) hides negative values).
uploadClip swallows errors and never retries, so the idempotency on seq is never used by the client. A lost clip is gone.
/api/percia/frames/{frame_id} is unauthenticated (relies on an unguessable uuid). That is acceptable for the portal but should be noted.
dev_video reads the whole video (up to 400 MB) into memory and runs a probe on a temp copy. OK for dev only.
Percia worker: frames list is capped at MAX_FRAMES=24. A 43 s clip therefore samples about 1 frame every 1.8 s, not 1 fps, which is fine but differs from the spec.
Callback verification uses only PERCIA_KEY, while Percia signs with the key that created the goal. This only works while the Itemizer always uses PERCIA_KEY (true today).
